Answer: B
Reason: The clinical history describes consolidations that resolved in one area (left upper lobe) and appeared in new areas (right upper lobe, left lower lobe) over two weeks despite antibiotic treatment; this pattern of "migratory infiltrates" unresponsive to antibiotics is the hallmark radiographic feature of Cryptogenic Organizing Pneumonia (COP). While the tool report for Figure 2 mentions nodules/cavitation (which may be hallucinated or misinterpreted), the explicit textual description in the question prompt regarding the temporal migration of consolidation takes precedence for diagnosis.
